drivers.driver: The business continues to demonstrate durable consumer loyalty and high-margin services growth
Management remains disciplined in capital return through share repurchases and dividends
The tax burden of selling a highly successful, long-term holding outweighs the benefits of a full exit at current prices

final.memo:
the Company remains, in my view, the best business I know [D08]. While the stock currently trades at a full valuation of approximately 33.75 times trailing earnings, we do not sell wonderful businesses simply because Mr. Market has become enthusiastic [D04]. The fundamental thesis—a powerful consumer ecosystem supported by a record installed base—remains firmly intact [D01, D05].

We recognize the risks posed by shifting trade policy and the potential for increased costs, such as the estimated $900 million tariff impact for the June quarter [D03, D05]. However, these are manageable near-term pressures rather than a fundamental erosion of the company's competitive advantage [D05]. Management continues to allocate capital intelligently, as evidenced by the recent $100 billion repurchase authorization and dividend increase [D03].

Finally, we must consider the tax consequences of reducing our position. A sale of this magnitude would trigger a significant federal tax liability, requiring the proceeds to be reinvested in an equally compelling opportunity to justify the friction [D04, D08]. Given the strength of the underlying business and the lack of a more attractive immediate alternative, we prefer to maintain our significant ownership [D08].
